extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in scientific machine learning / computational physics developing or evaluating PINNs
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and desiderata for designing, implementing, analyzing, and deploying Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to solve differential equations and related scientific-machine-learning tasks. Focuses on theoretical properties, implementation choices, optimization, and application constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergence to correct PDE solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PINN converges to the correct solution of the differential equation; approximation errors must tend to zero to achieve stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influenced by network topology and training procedure; existing outcomes are limited and require further theoretical study (examples: Mo et al [115], Mishra and Molinaro [111]). Evaluate convergence empirically across topologies and analyze approximator error behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability (approximation error tending to zero)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability criterion requiring approximation errors to vanish (tend to zero) for stable PINN solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depends on neural network architecture and representation capacity. Stability analyses are sparse; assess via error estimates and sensitivity to architecture changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation error / expressivity of NN architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: The neural network architecture defines how well the NN can approximate the target function; the residual difference is approximation error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test different architectures (depth/width, activation, special nets) and measure approximation error; consider theoretical approximation results and representational limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization error and loss-definition impact
rubrics_metrics.description: How the loss definition and the number/placement of points integrated into the loss affect generalization (ability to predict unseen domain regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure generalization error separately from empirical loss; investigate quadrature-based vs collocation-based loss estimation and sensitivity to point sampling strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization error (quality of minimization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effectiveness of the optimization algorithm in minimizing the PINN loss and the resulting optimization error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare optimizers (Adam, L-BFGS-B, etc.), study convergence behavior, optimizer-induced dynamics (gradient flow), and multiple restarts to assess robustness and failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency bias / F-principle and multiscale behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PINNs (and DNNs) tend to fit low-frequency components first (F-principle); therefore multi-scale or high-frequency solutions may be learned slowly or poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate performance on problems with multi-scale, chaotic, or turbulent behavior; consider architectural or training adaptations to capture high-frequency components (e.g., SIRENs, specialized activations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of initialization and loss function on learning and generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialization schemes and the specific loss function formulation affect learning dynamics and generalization error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically vary initializations and loss formulations; review literature for theoretical insights and quantify sensitivity to initialization across runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collocation point selection strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for choosing collocation/training points (random IID, quadrature rules, targeted regions) used to estimate PDE residuals and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare random sampling vs targeted selection in space-time regions (e.g., [118]); assess impact on accuracy and convergence; consider adaptive or problem-aware sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic loss weighting / balancing multiple loss terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring different loss components (PDE residual, initial/boundary data terms, data-fitting terms) are balanced — a NN will focus on the largest loss terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply dynamic reweighting strategies (gradient normalization, adaptive weighting) to keep loss terms of similar magnitude; evaluate effects on convergence and solution quality ([120], [119]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture exploration beyond FFNNs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration and evaluation of network families other than feedforward nets (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, FNO, N–BEATS, SIRENs) for PINN tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test alternative architectures for problem-specific advantages (e.g., long-range dependencies with Transformers, spectral structure with FNO, sinusoidal signals with SIRENs); measure representational gains and training cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation function choice and scalable activations
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and tuning of activation functions (including learnable/scalable activations) to improve convergence rate and solution correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate tunable activations (Jagtap et al [70]) and their effect on convergence and derivative estimation; include activation hyperparameter search in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of differentiation method (automatic vs numerical vs coupled)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method used to compute derivatives for PDE residuals — automatic differentiation (AD), numerical differentiation, or coupled automatic–numerical differentiation (CAN-PINN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sample efficiency and accuracy trade-offs: CAN-PINN may be more sample-efficient and accurate when AD alone requires many collocation points (Chiu et al [33]). Benchmark methods on target PDEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling boundary and initial conditions (soft vs hard enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: How initial/boundary conditions are enforced: as soft loss terms in training or hard-coded into the network architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate solution accuracy and robustness when using soft (loss penalty) versus hard (architectural encoding) enforcement; note that boundary-condition changes typically require retraining when enforced hard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss-term magnitude normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalization of individual loss components so no single term dominates optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize or rescale loss terms to comparable magnitudes; failing to do so can cause neglect of some constraints and poor solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective methods for determining loss weights (or lack thereof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there exists an objective, principled method to set weights for different loss components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes absence of an objective method; evaluations should report chosen weighting schemes and sensitivity analyses; prioritize adaptive weighting or theoretically-motivated schemes where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization algorithm selection and study (Adam, L-BFGS-B, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice, configuration, and analysis of optimization algorithms for PINN training (e.g., Adam, BFGS, L-BFGS-B) and their dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare practical performance and theoretical dynamics (gradient descent view, stiffness). L-BFGS-B is commonly used; study learning rate effects and optimizer-specific convergence behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of learning rate and gradient normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of learning rate schedules and gradient normalization techniques on PINN training behavior and convergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically vary learning rates and test gradient normalization/adaptive schemes to address stiffness and balance multi-term losses ([120]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Error estimation and provable bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and quality of error estimators (upper/lower bounds) quantifying PINN prediction error for ODEs/PDEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and validate error estimators (Hillebrecht & Unger [62]); extend toy examples to PDEs and derive lower bounds; include estimator-validation in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding or understanding curse of dimensionality / scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of PINN scaling properties in high-dimensional PDEs and explanation of why PINNs may avoid exponential cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically measure computational cost with increasing dimension; refer to theoretical works showing possibility of avoiding curse (Bauer & Kohler [13]) and quadrature-based approaches (Zubov et al [202]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior in modern learning-theory regimes (bias-variance, double descent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding PINN behavior in contexts like bias-variance trade-off and double-descent risk curves for rich/interpolating models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate function class H for the hypothesis space and how PINNs exhibit double-descent or interpolation behavior (Belkin et al [14]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft PDE-constraint optimization failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that PINNs can fail due to soft enforcement of PDE constraints rather than expressivity limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design loss formulations or training regimes to mitigate soft-constraint failures (Krishnapriyan et al [86]); test alternative formulations like sequence-to-sequence or causality-aware losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample efficiency: number and placement of training points
rubrics_metrics.description: How many collocation/training points are needed and where they should be placed for accurate PINN solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark sample-efficiency across problems; consider adaptive enrichment, ensemble-based point selection, and targeted sampling in regions of high residual or interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training-procedure design and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of the training protocol (schedules, optimizer switching, adaptive sampling, restarts) tailored to each physical problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and compare training pipelines; include ablation studies of choices (optimizer, batch size, learning rate schedule, dynamic weighting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-normalization / adimensionalization of PDEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescaling and nondimensionalization of physical problems prior to PINN training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-normalize variables to improve numerical conditioning and training stability; use symbolic tooling (e.g., SymPy) to help represent PDEs consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability with legacy scientific codes and HPC
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to integrate PINNs with existing Fortran/C/C++ scientific programs, legacy HPC applications, and distributed training tools (Horovod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate integration effort, communication overhead, and distributed training scalability; account for GPU memory limits and batch-size constraints for large 3D problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time / online-offline deployment feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility of using trained PINNs for rapid real-time evaluations (online) after potentially expensive offline training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure inference speed vs traditional solvers and training amortization; evaluate PINN utility in digital twin or control applications where fast inference is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling stiff problems and relation to numerical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological requirements for PINNs to solve stiff PDE/ODE problems and the need for theoretical foundations linking PINNs to numerical analysis and dynamical-systems theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study stiffness effects on gradient dynamics, optimization, and accuracy; consider specialized training/representation choices and theoretical analyses of stiffness impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and safety considerations for critical domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for rigorous stability analysis and theoretical guarantees before applying PINNs in safety-critical domains (healthcare, control, structural analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require provable error bounds, robustness testing, and thorough validation in domain-specific scenarios; emphasize theory and verification before deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-scale and high-frequency limitation assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of PINN ability to capture multi-scale phenomena and high-frequency solution components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark PINNs on multi-scale/climate/chaotic problems (noted limitations) and explore remedies (architecture, loss weighting, adaptive sampling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative function representations (kernel / Gaussian processes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of non-NN representations (kernel methods, Gaussian processes, NTK, GPyTorch) as alternatives or complements to PINNs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare expressivity, uncertainty quantification, and computational trade-offs; consider infinite-width NTK analyses and GPyTorch for GP-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth vs width trade-offs and minimum network size
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing whether increasing width or depth yields better PINN performance and whether a minimum depth/width is required to capture the physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimentally investigate breadth vs depth scaling; reference theory on width/depth benefits and test for problem-specific thresholds below which learning fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of network size (hyperparameter tuning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing the number of layers and neurons (network size) appropriate for the PDE/problem at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform hyperparameter sweeps, cross-validation, and sensitivity analyses; report how network size affects approximation, generalization, and training cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PINNs as linear solvers and comparisons to classical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of PINNs when used as linear solvers (e.g., Poisson equation) and comparison with high-performance solvers like PETSc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark accuracy and runtime vs established solvers; consider training cost and whether PINN provides competitive or complementary advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D problem challenges: representation capacity, GPU memory, training time
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations for scaling PINNs from 2D to 3D: need for larger representation capacity, batch-size/GPU-memory constraints, and longer training times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for hardware limits in experimental design; measure how GPU memory and batch-size restrictions impact convergence and consider distributed/HPC strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagation of initial/boundary information and causality-aware training
rubrics_metrics.description: How well PINNs propagate information from initial/boundary conditions into interior or future times; training algorithms should respect physical causation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use causality-aware loss formulations (Wang et al [180]) or sequence-to-sequence formulations to improve propagation; evaluate on problems requiring long-time prediction or chaotic dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble agreement and adaptive inclusion of new points
rubrics_metrics.description: Using ensemble agreement as a criterion for incorporating new points into the loss: ensemble members should agree near observed data and disagree far away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement ensemble-based adaptive sampling to add points where ensemble members diverge; assess convergence improvements and avoid overfitting to noisy observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of large PDE coefficients on loss landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity of PINN loss landscape and learnability when PDE coefficients (e.g., convection or viscosity) are large, potentially making problems hard to learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test PINNs on diffusion–convection problems and high-coefficient regimes (Krishnapriyan et al [86]); consider re-formulations or alternative training tasks (sequence-to-sequence) for robustness.
